🤖 THREEHALVES — THE CENTAUR ROBOT Threehalves is a 7-foot-tall teleoperated robot developed by Satyress. Its design combines a human-like torso and arms with a powerful four-legged chassis, creating a mechanical centaur built for environments that are too dangerous for humans. The idea behind Threehalves is simple: instead of sending a person into extreme heat, unstable terrain, darkness, hazardous industrial environments or disaster zones, a skilled operator can control the robot remotely and perform the work from a safer location. Unlike many humanoid robots, Threehalves is designed around tools and equipment that humans already use. Its modular limbs and quick-connect system allow it to be adapted for different tasks, while its four-legged platform provides stability on difficult terrain. The most unsettling part is probably its appearance. With its enormous size, humanoid body, four mechanical legs and distinctive horned head, Threehalves looks less like a traditional industrial machine and more like something from a science-fiction horror movie. But behind the terrifying design is a serious engineering concept: putting the machine in danger instead of the human. Threehalves is still a developing robotics project, but it represents a strange glimpse into a future where dangerous jobs could be performed remotely — with a human controlling the machine from a distance. And honestly… it might be one of the creepiest robots ever built. 👁️ #threehalves #robot #baal #satyress #horrortok

Chinese humanoid robots broke records set by humans, including Usain Bolt's 100m sprint world record, on the opening day of the Olympics-like World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing on Saturday. More than 2,000 humanoid robots were participating in the event, organisers said. In a 100-metre sprint, a humanoid robot achieved a result of 9.39 seconds, beating the human record of 9.58 seconds set by Jamaican athlete Bolt in 2009. In a standing high jump, a humanoid robot was able to reach 2.88m, well above the 0.95m best result by a humanoid in last year’s first edition of the games. It surpassed the human high jump record of 2.45m set by Cuba’s Javier Sotomayor in 1993. The five-day games, now in their second year, are a spectacle demonstrating China’s rapid progress in advanced robotics as the technology race with the US heats up. There are 51 events and more than 1,000 competitions taking place, including running, table tennis and football. For more news, visit @sbsnews_au (link in bio).

videos.caption: China's HOUSEHOLD ROBOT Does Laundry, Cooks and Makes Your Bed by 2027 #news #technology #china #robot  GigaAI has unveiled the SeeLight S1, China's first general purpose household humanoid robot, and it is coming to real homes as early as 2027. Built with embodied AI, the two armed wheeled robot can chop vegetables, fry eggs, load a washing machine, hang laundry, make a bed and open curtains autonomously, no pre programmed routines required. One hundred units begin trialing at Wuhan tech worker housing this month, with free pilot deployments targeting families with elderly members, children or pets launching in the first half of 2027. GigaAI is targeting a retail price below 100,000 yuan, roughly 14,700 US dollars, by mid 2027, cutting the current cost in half. The company expects major commercialisation milestones and breakthroughs in household AI model capabilities by 2028. China's LIFELIKE Robot Face Will Make You Question Everything #news #technology #china #robot  Chinese startup AheadForm has built a humanoid robot head that is nearly impossible to distinguish from a real human face. Powered by thirty precision brushless micro motors embedded beneath bionic silicone skin, the robot controls every blink, every glance, and every subtle micro expression with stunning accuracy. Cameras integrated directly into the eyes allow the robot to track faces in real time, while an onboard AI system reads human emotions and responds instantly with matching expressions. This is not a CGI render or a movie prop. This is real technology being developed right now in China for deployment in customer service, healthcare, and personal companionship. A viral video of the robot posted in March 2026 reignited a global conversation about whether hyper realistic robot faces are the missing key to making humanoid robots commercially successful. AheadForm believes the future of human robot interaction depends not just on what robots can do, but on how real they feel. The face of the future just got a lot harder to spot.

It originated in the Tang Dynasty, with its predecessor being the "Xiqin" played by northern ethnic minorities. Although its structure is simple — a wooden sound box covered with python skin at the front, a neck standing upright on it, and two strings sounded by a bow — it possesses great acoustic wisdom. I spent days teaching a 3D-printed robot duck to walk. Most of that time, it was falling over. It’s my own build of the Open Duck Mini. The open-source, BDX-inspired biped created by Antoine Pirrone. The whole thing is 3D-printed and runs on hobby-grade servos instead of industrial actuators, which is what makes it buildable on a normal budget and also what makes it so hard to get walking. The hard part wasn’t the printing or the assembly. It was the sim-to-real gap. A gait that walks perfectly in MuJoCo hits real-world joint slop, servo lag, and a center of mass that won’t sit still, and just before you know it, the duck face plants into the floor. It took me 40+ calibration passes before it could take three steps without tipping! What the build came down to: • 3D-printed chassis • Per-joint offset calibration (where most of the pain lived) • Policy training in simulation (MuJoCo / Isaac Lab) • Build guide + docs via Tnkr • A lot of failed walks Real hardware. Real failures. Real progress.

Industrial humanoid robots are looking less humanlike every day.  The Chinese company LimX Dynamics just shared footage of its TRON 2 dual-arm robot integrated with an industrial robotic arm. The TRON 2 multi-form-factor robot has gone viral in the past for its modular design that can transform into a humanoid, a quadruped, or even be combined into a centaur.    In the industrial setup, TRON 2 is mounted onto a traditional robotic arm to extend its reach. It uses a custom attachment to hold and operate a power drill and nailer to assemble wooden frames and panels. It then applies spray finishing.    The TRON 2 is priced starting around $7,000 in China but international pricing begins around $13,000. Meet NEXi Version 3 🤖✨ NEXi Version 3 is my latest AI-powered desktop robot, designed to be an interactive companion with its own personality. Built around the ESP32-S3-N8R2 and a 1.3-inch OLED display, it combines AI, animations, and smart sensors in a compact custom-designed robot. Unlike NEXi Version 2, this version doesn't move on wheels and doesn't include a camera. Instead, it focuses on expressive interactions. NEXi can communicate using AI, remember conversations, answer questions, and react naturally to different situations. The robot features an MPU6050 motion sensor, allowing it to detect movement and respond when it's picked up or shaken. It also includes a touch sensor, so NEXi can react differently when you tap or gently interact with it. These features make the robot feel much more alive and responsive, even while staying on your desk. Everything—from the electronics and software to the custom 3D-printed design—was developed from scratch. NEXi Version 3 proves that a desktop robot doesn't need to move around to be intelligent, interactive, and full of personality.
